subject.title: [Feature]: Add runtime testing for skill workshop proposals before apply

question: What pre-apply runtime validation contract should Skill Workshop expose, and which generated-skill invocation side effects must be skipped, sandboxed, or explicitly allowed?
rationale: The missing source surface is clear, but running pending proposal content before apply creates a product and security boundary across tool policy, network access, filesystem writes, Gateway API shape, and proposal health semantics.

options.title: Load/schema-only MVP
options.body: Add a first version that verifies proposed skill discovery, loading, and schema visibility while marking invocation and behavior checks as skipped until a side-effect contract exists.

options.title: Full safe invocation contract
options.body: Define proposal-provided inputs, expected outputs, allowed side effects, and isolated tool execution before adding runtime invocation and apply gating.

options.title: Fold into broader dry-run design
options.body: Keep this open but implement it only after the broader skills/cron/tool dry-run contract is settled in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/13617.

recommendation.title: Load/schema-only MVP
recommendation.body: Add a first version that verifies proposed skill discovery, loading, and schema visibility while marking invocation and behavior checks as skipped until a side-effect contract exists.

likelyOwner.reason: shakkernerd introduced the central Skill Workshop service and proposal model that this validation gate would extend.
